This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V.Act') has been filed against award dated 11/04/2017 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District - Balod (CG) in Claim Case No.65/2016.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District - Balod (CG)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32671 2.

By the impugned award, learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.7,73,000/- in favour of the claimants as compensation on account of death of Hemant Kumar Mandavi in an unfortunate accident that took place on 17/02/2016 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle (Bore Vehicle-Truck) bearing registration No. MH-17C-5700.
A claim application claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.31,00,000/- was filed by the claimants which was resisted by the respondents - driver, owner and the insurance company.

Learned Tribunal, after framing issues, decided the same in favour of the claimants and awarded compensation as stated above and the driver, owner and the insurance company were jointly held liable to pay the compensation.
As per claim application, the deceased was earning Rs.11,000/- per month working as Head Mistry and was aged about 21 years.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants submits that the finding recorded by the learned Tribunal is bad in law.
The monthly income has been wrongly assessed by the learned Tribunal and compensation on other heads is also on the lower side.
Therefore, the finding is perverse and is liable to be set aside.
4. Learned counsel for respondents 1 and 2 support the award.

5. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 submits that appellants No.3 to 5 are not dependents and appellants 4 and 5 are married sisters of the deceased and they are living seperately and appellant No.3 / brother is also working.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the records.

7. Looking to the evidence available and also taking guidance from the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation and ors., (2009)
6 SCC 121, National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi and ors, (2017) 16 SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., (2018) 18 SCC 130, this Court hereby computes the compensation in the following manner - 1 Monthly income Rs.6000/-
2 Future Prospects 40% Rs.8400/-

8.
The learned Tribunal awarded Rs.7,73,000/- which is deducted from the total compensation now assessed and the enhanced compensation comes to Rs.3,64,200/-.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, interest @ 6% is also awarded on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of filing of the claim application to be deposited within a period of 60 days.
After deposit, Rs.50,000/- each shall be paid to appellant No.2 to 5.
Rs. 1 lakh shall be invested in a nationalised bank as fixed deposit in the name of appellant No.1 and 2 for two years.
Remaining amount shall be paid to appellant No.2 through bank transaction/account payee cheque.
9. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed.
